auto_false_positive.reason: STUN binding request/response - normal NAT traversal traffic, used by Tailscale, WebRTC, VoIP, gaming.
ET DOS Possible SSDP Amplification Scan - internal UDP discovery to port 1900 is normal SSDP/UPnP traffic, not an external amplification attack.
ET SCAN NMAP -sA - scoped to inbound TCP response traffic from source port 443 to an internal client, the common false-positive shape for the return half of HTTPS connections.
Discord client traffic - normal usage of Discord domains observed in TLS SNI/HTTPS. The 'Observed Discord Domain' signatures fire on every Discord connection and produce zero security signal.
Public DNS-over-HTTPS providers (Google 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1). Normal DNS traffic from any modern browser or DNS-over-HTTPS-aware client. ET INFO rules track observed DoH usage, not threats.
Android device connectivity check - every Android phone makes these requests every few minutes to detect captive portals. ET INFO informational rule, not a threat.
Microsoft connectivity test - Windows checks msftncsi.com / connectivitycheck endpoints to detect internet/captive portal status. ET INFO informational rule.
External IP lookup services (ipinfo.io, ip-api.com). Used by browsers, scripts, and tools that need to know their public IP. Benign except in extreme cases of unusual frequency.
Steam HTTP client User-Agent. Normal Steam client traffic for game updates, friends list, store browsing.
Spotify P2P client behavior. Normal Spotify desktop usage.

Legacy ET MALWARE Conficker/KEYPLUG P2P UDP signatures (2009-era) match modern STUN traffic to Microsoft Azure STUN servers (20.202.0.0/16:3478) used by Teams, Xbox Live, Skype, and Tailscale DERP relays. Confirmed false positive: same UDP packet shape, different intent. v0.2 Foundation-Sec with category-aware prompting still misclassifies these because the prompt's ET MALWARE default-to-real rule overrides STUN-context recognition (149 alerts tested, 100% misclassified as real). v0.3 RAG layer with signature-specific context should resolve this; until then, prefilter.
STUN binding on non-standard high port - same NAT traversal mechanism, different rule pattern.
DNS NXDOMAIN response - benign DNS lookup failure (typo'd domains, browser prefetch, Pi-hole blocks). DGA-style abuse is caught separately by SID 2008470.
Go HTTP client user agent - normal traffic from Go-based services in the homelab (containers, internal tools, CI/CD agents).
Discord chat service traffic - normal Discord usage from desktop/mobile clients.

Suricata decoder event for unknown EtherType - emitted when Suricata sees layer-2 frames it can't classify (often VLAN tags, MPLS, IPv6 extensions, or vendor-specific protocols). Decoder noise, not a security signal. Confirmed across thousands of samples in homelab traffic — 100% false positive rate via LLM classification.
Spotify P2P client traffic - normal Spotify desktop client peer-to-peer caching behavior.
Linux APT user-agent outbound - normal package update traffic (apt update / apt upgrade) from homelab Linux servers.
Python BaseHTTP server banner - homelab Python services exposing their default banner. Internal traffic, not an exposure risk on a private network.
